### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via AutomationContext (symbol, a top-level interface), FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx`  _(via AutomationContext (symbol, a top-level interface))_

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via AutomationContext (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class), FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via AutomationContext (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via AutomationContext (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2667e2402c48e9201550caca2adbcf9188d925b3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `df62bbd6883aedb7a97d1f52e7c8758e90514441` — the merge of head `e5150923a095f4f77dcbc60486d1594fd2541a63` into base `2667e2402c48e9201550caca2adbcf9188d925b3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin df62bbd6883aedb7a97d1f52e7c8758e90514441 && git checkout df62bbd6883aedb7a97d1f52e7c8758e90514441
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2667e2402c48e9201550caca2adbcf9188d925b3 e5150923a095f4f77dcbc60486d1594fd2541a63 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2667e2402c48e9201550caca2adbcf9188d925b3 && git merge --no-ff e5150923a095f4f77dcbc60486d1594fd2541a63

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2667e2402c48e9201550caca2adbcf9188d925b3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2667e2402c48e9201550caca2adbcf9188d925b3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Head-sha: `c17394ee557a1bf653988500254d3ba6a61e544b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/runtime-identity.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/resume-decider-identity.integration.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/package.json, packages/services/service-automation/vitest.config.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/restored-approval-continuation.test.ts, pnpm-lock.yaml, .changeset/24321-resume-as-decider.md, content/docs/references/automation/flow.mdx, content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts, packages/rest/src/approvals-routes.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-request.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/index.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts, content/docs/automation/flows.mdx, content/docs/ui/actions.mdx

Read at 2026-10-19T14:47Z on PR #24527 (draft, head repo = base repo), card #24321 (body and all twelve comments: ruling A `6257886738`, the claim `6264284385`, the round-0 report `6267118015`, the return question `6267218798`, the director delta `6267456613`, the ruling `6267719791` Q1 A · Q2 A, the patch-round report `6269555250`, the elevation-pull note `6269649076`), the PR body and its one comment (the docs-drift advisory), the 13-file list, the net diff against merge base `04669a467` (+994 −42), and the 49 check-runs on the head — all completed, none in progress. The five required contexts are `success`: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core (and its six shards), Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard. Also `success`: Check Changeset (twice, the second after the body edit), Validate Package Dependencies, Spec property liveness, Build Docs, and the four card/branch claim checks. The `skipped` rows are matrix placeholders and full-battery-only jobs (Console Pin Gate, Temporal Conformance, dogfood shards, the packed-tarball opt-in), skipped on PR runs by design. Nothing was built, run or re-run locally; the two repo scripts used are the record template and the posting tool.

### ① Derived judgments

Each judged against the code at the head, not against the reports.

1. **`runAs: 'user'` continues as the decider, identity and grants together — right.** `AutomationEngine.resolveDecisionSegmentContext` (engine.ts) takes a COPY of the persisted `run.context`, sets `userId` to the decider, records `triggerUserId`, deletes `positions`, `permissions` and `org_user_ids`, and calls `seedRunGrants(run.flowName, switched, 'deciding')` — the same method `resolveRunContext` calls with `'triggering'` at run setup, so the decider's grants come from the one wired `userGrantsResolver` (positions, permission sets, peers; `tenantId` back-filled only when absent). `seedRunGrants` resolves nothing for `runAs: 'system'`, a user-less context, a context already carrying every fact, or an engine with no resolver; a resolver throw is caught and warned, and the segment then runs on the baseline member set — narrower, never the submitter's grants (pinned). `resolveRunDataContext`'s user arm hands ObjectQL exactly `userId`, `positions`, `permissions`, `org_user_ids`, `tenantId`, `flowRunId`, so nothing of the trigger user's reaches a post-decision write. A decider who already is the acting user is a no-op. One corner, named and right under ruling A item 1: a `runAs: 'user'` run whose trigger resolved no user (its pre-decision data ops are refused) runs its post-decision nodes as the decider — the decider is the human whose act runs that segment.
2. **`runAs: 'system'` keeps elevation and carries `{ isSystem: true, userId: DECIDER }`, no grant resolved — right** (ruling `6267719791` Q1 A). The same deletions and `userId` switch, then `if (switched.runAs === 'system') return switched;` BEFORE `seedRunGrants`. `resolveRunDataContext`'s system arm emits `isSystem: true`, `actor: svc:flow:NAME`, the context's `userId` and `tenantId`, `positions: []`, `permissions: []` — so elevation is untouched, the readonly column still lands, and `updated_by`, `sys_audit_log.user_id` and hook `ctx.user` name the decider (pinned on the real stack with AuditPlugin). The ObjectQL envelope of a system run never carried positions, so deleting the forwarded ones changes only the CEL `current_user` (`runUserOf` reads `userId`, `positions`, `tenantId`): after the decision a system run's `current_user.positions` is `[]` where a door-forwarded trigger's positions used to ride. That is inside Q1 A's letter (no permission resolution) and the honest shape — the alternative is the decider's id over the submitter's positions. Named for the seat; not a defect.
3. **Only approve and reject carry a decider — right** (Q2 A). `decide()` is the single producer: `resumedBy: actingUserId(context)`, the authenticated caller's `userId` or `null`. Recall, the revision-limit auto-reject, send-back and resubmit call `serviceResume` / `resumeRecordedOutcome` with no `resumedBy`. The SLA sweep calls `decide(..., SYSTEM_CTX)`, so `actingUserId` is `null` and the run keeps its identity (pinned). The action link passes `{ ...SYSTEM_CTX, userId: person }`, so its decider is the token's person. The verdict mirror is written with `mirrorStatusField(..., actingUserId(context))` (approval-service.ts:4002) — the same expression — so "the person the verdict mirror already writes as" holds by construction on every door.
4. **A flow with no decision node, and an SLA decision, are unchanged — right.** `resolveDecisionSegmentContext` returns `run.context` unchanged when the signal names no decider or lacks the marker; every engine-built continuation (`engineBuilt`, `buildSubflowResumeSignal`) carries neither. Subflow-hosted approval: the parent frame forwards the caller's signal to the child (which holds the approval node and switches), then reassigns `signal = this.buildSubflowResumeSignal(childRun.context, childRes.output)` before reaching its own switch, so the parent keeps its context — the PR's acceptance note is accurate. The degraded "child run is gone — continuing without child output" branch keeps the caller's signal, so there the parent would switch to the decider; a degraded path, consistent with ruling A's reading, noted.
5. **Authority of `resumedBy` — right; no caller outside the owning service can make the engine honour a decider.** `RESUME_AUTHORITY_SERVICE` is `Symbol.for('objectstack.automation.resume.service')` (spec `contracts/automation-service.ts:585`). Setters at the head, outside tests: exactly one, `ApprovalService.serviceResume` (approval-service.ts:4045), which every approvals-side resume goes through. Readers: `refuseGatedResume` (engine.ts:7375, the #3801 gate) and `resolveDecisionSegmentContext` (engine.ts:6595, `signal[RESUME_AUTHORITY_SERVICE] === true ? signal.resumedBy : undefined`). The REST resume door (`runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`, `RESUME_BODY_KEYS = ['inputs', 'variables', 'output', 'branchLabel']`) answers 400 on a `resumedBy` key; a JSON body or header cannot carry a symbol-keyed property in any case; and an `approval` pause is refused at that door before anything (`resumeAuthority: 'service'`). The REST approve/reject door hands `decide` the authenticated `resolveExecCtx` context, with the body's `actorId` a hint the service pins to the caller. A script holding the import (or `Symbol.for` with the string) can mint the marker — that is in-process code, the trust level that can already write with `isSystem: true`; the TSDoc and the published CHANGELOG state that scope. The journalled decider rides `sys_approval_request.node_config_json`, a `readonly: true` column objectql strips from every non-system update, and `continueRestoredRun` is an in-process operator verb with no REST or MCP route. Controls pinned: a decider without the marker, and a marker without a decider, change nothing.
6. **The persisted run and its replays — right; the history still names the trigger user.** A later pause persists the switched context (`persistSuspendedRun({ ...run, context, ... })` at the re-suspend site), so a second decision, a cold resume or a no-decider continuation never falls back to the submitter; a second decider replaces the first and `triggerUserId` is kept (`runTriggerUserId(context) ?? null`, read back through `hasOwnProperty`, and `null` survives the JSON round trip). The engine's strand journal snapshots the pre-switch `run.context` (never mutated) and the approvals journal carries `resumedBy`, so `continueRestoredRun` re-applies the switch (pinned). `buildRunTrigger` reads `runTriggerUserId`, `recordLog` stamps the row with `trigger.userId`, and the REST starter gate `isRunStarterOrRunStateReader` compares `run.trigger.userId` — the trigger user keeps run visibility, the decider gains none. A strand journalled before this release carries no `resumedBy` and replays as the trigger user: a one-release transitional corner, stated in the PR; acceptable.
7. **The two new devDependencies — right; test-only.** `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` and `@objectstack/plugin-audit` sit under `devDependencies` in `service-automation/package.json` (its `dependencies` are unchanged: core, formula, metadata-core, metadata-protocol, platform-objects, spec, types); the lockfile gains the two `link:` entries and nothing else; the anchored-regex vitest aliases read them from source; the only importer is the new integration test. No runtime edge. `Validate Package Dependencies` is `success`.
8. **The published-surface names are right.** `ApprovalResumeSurface` and `StrandedContinuationSignal` are exported types of `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` (its `index.ts`), and `ResumeSignal` of `@objectstack/spec/contracts`, so the three optional members the Clause-② line names are published widenings. `resolveRunDataContext` is a public export of `@objectstack/service-automation` (its `index.ts`), so the cross-package test import is sound.

### ② Semver level

Right. The changeset bumps exactly the three packages whose published source moves — `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, all published at `18.0.0-next.5` — each `minor`; the title carries the bang (`feat(automation)!:`); the body carries the **BREAKING** banner; one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, whose argument is correct (no key, export, option, enum value or stored shape is removed, renamed or re-shaped; `triggerUserId` and the journal's `resumedBy` are additive); and `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` in both the changeset and the PR body — `yes` for the three optional members on published interfaces, `(narrowing)` for the post-decision refusal under the decider's rights. AGENTS.md's rule holds: `yes` takes at least `minor`, `(narrowing)` is BREAKING, and the migration text ("What changes for you") is present. The seven regenerated `runAs` rows in the two reference pages match the describe byte-for-byte; the api-surface snapshot is unaffected (members, not exports); `Check Changeset` and `TypeScript Type Check` (which carries every spec gate) are `success`. The PR is not a fork, is a draft, touches no governed path, and changes 1,036 lines.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (`deviations`), round-0 report `6267118015` and patch round `6269555250`:
- "Part of" vs "Fixes" — resolved by ruling `6267719791` item 3; the body's first line is `Fixes #24321` and the two card/branch claim checks re-ran `success` after the edit.
- Clause-② kept `no (narrowing)` for re-grade — re-graded to `yes (narrowing)` as the ruling directs; verified in both carriers (② above).
- `contracts/automation-service.ts` beyond the describe — declared to the spec seat in the PR body's "Spec-lane files"; it is a `reviewFace` hit here and is read in ① (items 5 and 8).
- `plugin-sharing` and `plugin-audit` devDependencies and vitest aliases — judged test-only (① item 7); `check:test-source-alias` and `check:cross-package-test-inputs` ride in Lint & Repo Gates, `success`.
- Pins placed in the existing `restored-approval-continuation.test.ts` — fine; `check:engine-double-contract` is in the green union.
- `runtime-identity.ts` touched — needed (`SeededRunContext.triggerUserId`, `runTriggerUserId`); TSDoc corrected where the change made it false — right, and the system arm's text now matches the code.
- The system switch also removes forwarded positions, permission sets and peers — right, with the `current_user.positions` corner named in ① item 2.
- Two `os-regen-merge.sh` merges, the throwaway real-door measurement file in `packages/verify` (absent from the file list), the model-free commit trailers, the changeset/PR-title alignment — all in order; this record judges the net diff only.
- `open_questions`: round 0's two are ruled (`6267719791`, Q1 A · Q2 A) and both are in the code (① items 2 and 3); the patch round lists none.
- `out_of_scope_findings` (carrier: none): the pre-release strand and the subflow parent — both read in ① (items 6 and 4) and found as stated.

The claim's exclusions hold on the diff: `approval-service.ts`'s hunks touch the `ApprovalResumeSurface` and `StrandedContinuationSignal` members and TSDoc, the `serviceResume` and `resumeRecordedOutcome` signatures, `decide`'s signal, the journal spread and the `continueRestoredRun` spread — no row builder and no hand-built `{ isSystem: true, userId }` write context (#24501, #24519); `packages/objectql/**`, `packages/core/**` and `docs/adr/**` are absent from the 13-file list.

**Found by this review — the one defect, and the reason for the verdict.** `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`, a hand-written page the docs-drift advisory on this PR named, still restates the rule this PR changes, and the PR does not touch it. The `runAs` row of its flow-key table (line 76) says `'user'` is "the triggering user, RLS-respecting" — a paraphrase of the OLD describe, now contradicted by the regenerated reference row. The "Who may resume" section (lines 1090–1091) says a resumed run's "data nodes run as the user who **started** it, whoever sent the values" — after this PR, a screen or wait pause reached after an approval decision continues as the DECIDER (the persisted context is the segment's), so that sentence is false in the multi-stage case; the caller gate it goes on to describe (`trigger.userId`) is still right. Under a BREAKING banner on exactly this key, the guide is an authoring trap on the narrowing's edge (Prime Directive #10, corollary): an author designing post-decision nodes from this page expects the submitter's rights. The fix is two sentences in a hand-written tree, editable in a code PR: make row 76 mirror the new describe, and make line 1090 read "the identity stored on the run — the user who started it, or, after an approval decision, the decider". `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx`, the other flagged page, speaks only of identity forwarding at the trigger door and stays true. Also noted, non-blocking: the header comment of `resume-decider-identity.integration.test.ts` names `plugin-approvals`' `decision-resume-decider.test.ts`, a file that does not exist at the head — the hand-off pins live in `restored-approval-continuation.test.ts`.

Every contract-level judgment above is right. The next head needs only the docs edit; ① and ② carry over to it unchanged unless the engine, approvals or spec files move.

**What moved since `c17394ee5`, verified on the objects, not the reports.** Two commits: `be9efd1c5` (two files, +4 −4) and the merge `e5150923a` of `origin/main` `2667e2402` (parents `be9efd1c5`, `2667e2402`). Blob-for-blob, twelve of the fourteen PR paths are identical to `c17394ee5`: the changeset, both regenerated reference pages, `approval-service.ts`, `restored-approval-continuation.test.ts`, `package.json`, `engine.ts`, `runtime-identity.ts`, `vitest.config.ts`, `flow.zod.ts`, `automation-service.ts`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
